title: Lessons from the States, Book IV, Ode 3: The Kün-zze Kieh Lâo
note:
Stanza 2 only, as Legge gives it.

Contrast between the beauty and splendour of Hsüan Kiang and her viciousness.

Hsüan Kiang was a princess of Khî, who, towards the close of the seventh century B.C., became wife to the marquis of Wei, known as duke Hsüan. She was beautiful and unfortunate, but various things are related of her indicative of the grossest immoralities prevailing in the court of Wei.

verses.t:
How rich and splendid
Is her pheasant-figured robe!
Her black hair in masses like clouds,
No false locks does she descend to.
There are her earplugs of jade,
Her comb-pin of ivory,
And her high forehead, so white.
She appears like a visitant from heaven!
She appears like a goddess.
